vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-rpg
Version: 1.0.1

The agent-rpg skill bundle is a well-structured toolkit for running text-based role-playing games. It includes Python scripts (context.py and dice.py) for state management and dice rolling, which operate locally within a designated memory directory and show no signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution.

llm.summary: This RPG skill mostly matches its stated purpose, but it needs Review because its save-file script can access files outside the intended campaign folder and its dice roller lacks resource limits.

dimensions.detail: Local filesystem access is proportionate for campaign saves, but the unvalidated campaign name permits path traversal outside memory/rpg, and dice expressions can request unbounded work.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency fetch, remote payload retrieval, tool wrapping, service creation, or network behavior was found in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Invocation is mostly RPG-specific, but the reference material includes ERP/adult roleplay guidance without clear user consent or safety boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent campaign files are disclosed in SKILL.md, but writes are not constrained to the documented directory and there is no clear opt-in, cleanup, or deletion guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill coherently describes a text RPG GM with persistent campaign state and dice utilities; the scripts provide local state management and dice rolling while the markdown supplies the GM behavior instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only simple campaign names such as letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores, and avoid saving sensitive personal content because campaign state is written to disk. The publisher should add path validation, dice limits, clear opt-in and deletion instructions, and remove or gate the adult-roleplay guidance.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the scripts are narrower than the full GM description, but the skill text itself provides the GM procedures and the scripts align with the advertised dice and persistent-state support.
[LP3] expected: Local campaign state files are expected for this skill, but the artifact does not enforce a least-privilege storage boundary in code.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation text is broad within RPG use, but it is not unrelated to the stated purpose; users should still expect persistence only when running a campaign.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent storage is explicitly documented under memory/rpg, though the skill would benefit from clearer consent and deletion instructions.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The ERP reference is not necessary for the state-management and dice-rolling purpose and lacks explicit safeguards.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: scripts/context.py joins user-controlled campaign names directly to memory/rpg, allowing traversal to fixed filenames outside the intended save directory.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: scripts/dice.py accepts unbounded dice counts and sides, which can cause excessive CPU or memory use from a crafted roll expression.
